title: Steven Galloway asks judge to declare rape allegations false as defamation trial enters final submissions
summary: Former University of British Columbia professor Steven Galloway is asking the presiding justice in his defamation trial to vindicate his reputation by making an explicit finding of "falsehood," which…

image.caption: Steven Galloway, back centre, is seen through a window as he leaves B.C. Supreme Court in Vancouver, on Tuesday, Oct. 6, 2026. The author alleges defamation against a former student with whom he had an extramarital affair, and three other defendants. (Darryl Dyck/THE CANADIAN PRESS)

blocks.text: British Columbia

Former University of British Columbia professor Steven Galloway is asking the presiding justice in his defamation trial to vindicate his reputation by making an explicit finding of "falsehood," which would essentially clear the author of the rape and sexual assault accusation levelled against him over a decade ago.
Former UBC prof undeserving of 'horrific stain' on his name for more than decade, says lawyer
Former University of British Columbia professor Steven Galloway is asking the presiding justice in his defamation trial to vindicate his reputation by making an explicit finding of "falsehood."

"There's been a horrific stain on his name for over a decade," said Galloway's lead counsel Daniel Burnett during closing submissions on Monday. "It's in the public interest to have a final resolution of these allegations that have floated around for so long."
Galloway alleges defamation against a former student with whom he had an extramarital affair, and three other defendants who repeated rape allegations online and elsewhere.

items: Sexual assault claims 'flat out never happened,' ex-UBC professor tells defamation trial

blocks.text: Galloway's main accuser, identified only as A.B. because of a publication ban, earlier withdrew her defence of justification, choosing not to argue that claims Galloway raped or sexually assaulted her on three occasions in 2011 were true. Justice Neena Sharma had said the woman had not admitted that her accusations are false and the court couldn't make assumptions until it hears all evidence.

A.B. is a former UBC graduate student who is five years older than Galloway. She did not appear or testify at trial because of mental health concerns. Three other defendants — Mandi Gray, Glynnis Kirchmeier and Dana Kagis — are alleged to have repeated A.B.'s claims on social media and elsewhere.

"It's an unfortunate reality in this day and age that truth can often end up being in the hands of those who shout the loudest, those who tweet the most and those who recruit the most allies. And the court trial process is the last stop," Burnett told Sharma.
Steven Galloway is pictured in his office at the University of British Columbia in Vancouver on March 31, 2014. (Ben Nelms/CBC)
A.B. brought her allegations to UBC in November 2015. Soon after, Galloway was suspended, a move the university announced publicly by citing "serious allegations" against him.
A retired judge hired by UBC to conduct an investigation found that on a balance of probabilities he had not committed sexual assault.
Galloway was fired for misconduct. He was never criminally investigated.

items: UBC prof testifies she acted as a 'conduit' for sex assault allegations against Steven Galloway

blocks.text: Burnett told the court there was "overwhelming evidence of deliberate and calculated falsehoods built upon falsehoods." He said A.B. ran a strategic campaign to leverage criminal accusations against Galloway through other people.

That included, Burnett said, A.B. lying to friends and UBC officials that her story would be featured on an episode of the CBC's fifth estate if UBC didn't act against Galloway, and that CBC lawyers had found her evidence of the rape to be damning.

Burnett said A.B.'s "fabrications" cast serious doubt on everything she said, citing a disturbing claim A.B. made about being possibly drugged into unconsciousness and violently raped by Galloway in his UBC office.

Burnett said text messages between A.B. and her ex-husband on the night in question, along with other inconsistencies in her account, demonstrated that the allegation was not simply false but a "knowing lie."

items: Defendant apologizes to B.C. writer days before defamation trial to start

blocks.text: The author of The Cellist of Sarajevo admitted during testimony that he and A.B. had an affair between 2011 and 2013 while both were married.
His defamation lawsuit filed in 2018 originally named more than 20 defendants, the majority of whom settled before the trial began. A number of the defendants have also issued public apologies.
Burnett said Galloway has endured loss and suffering since 2015 that no person should wish on another.
"Hopefully, the outcome of this case will — as far as any court decision can — enable him to recover something back and have a better future," said Burnett.
Defence's closing submissions are expected to begin Tuesday in B.C. Supreme Court in Vancouver.
